answer: Transitive credit networks deter Sybil attacks by restricting transactions to bilateral, collateralized channels. Viewed through the prism of network max-flow bounds, synthetic clusters cannot transact beyond credit granted by honest peers. An adversary seeking to harbor fake identities must commit scarce liquid capital per node, leaving automated swarms no haven from financial costs. However, channel depletion can exhaust routing liquidity, stranding honest participants during volume spikes.
